issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement specifies messageOnMilk() should return a String with the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (problem_statement.md), and the template Main prints the method's return value. In the reference solution, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() to return boolean, and Seal and Goat implement it by printing the message and returning true. This is a clear return-type and behavior mismatch: the specification and template imply a String-returning method that provides the printable message, while the solution provides a boolean-returning method that performs printing internally. This inconsistency will confuse students about the correct method signature and expected behavior and may cause tests or example code in the template to behave unexpectedly.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent design and apply it across artifacts. Recommended: change the Milkable interface method signature to return String (public interface Milkable { String messageOnMilk(); }) and update Seal and Goat to return the message string (e.g. return getClass().getSimpleName() + " " + getName() + " is milked";) without printing inside the method. Update any callers (e.g. Main) and tests to print or assert the returned String. Alternatively, if the boolean-returning design is intentional, update the problem statement and template to specify a boolean return and adjust examples to call a separate printing/formatting utility rather than relying on the method to return the printable message.
